Title: Update rollback reverts binaries but does not restore database compatibility or damaged data
Evidence: Desktop update installation is now data-aware. Electron disables install-on-quit and, before an explicit upgrade, stops the backend and runs the frozen backend in maintenance mode. Maintenance mode creates a validated SQLite snapshot in a version-specific directory, records the source and target application versions, source schema revision, snapshot filename and SHA-256 digest in an atomically written mode-0600 recovery journal, and permits installation only after that state is durable. A signed downgrade is accepted only when the journal contains the exact immediate-predecessor upgrade snapshot. Before restoring it, GODFIN preserves the current database in a separate safety directory; the restored database is validated and checked against its recorded schema revision. If the current build restarts before rollback installation completes, startup restores the preserved current database and marks the rollback aborted. If the predecessor starts, it marks the rollback complete before normal SQLite startup. Corrupt journals, missing or tampered snapshots, mismatched schema evidence, skipped-version rollback, and failed restore all fail closed. Release workflows generate a checksummed compatibility manifest, require 5/25/50/100 staged rollout confirmation, prevent advancing a different tag, verify both current and predecessor release sets, and reject a rollback that is not the declared immediate predecessor.
